question.text: A famous part of the army of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth were the Winged Hussars, an elite cavalry unit that lifted the Ottoman siege of this present-day European country's capital city of Vienna.
question.clue: This country's far-right Freedom Party was led by Jorg Haider (yerg "HI"-der).

swap.leadin: A meeting in this city was interrupted by Napoleon's escape from Elba.
swap.text: Name this host of an 1815 meeting that established the balance of power of Europe in the 19th century, the capital of Austria.
swap.clue: This city's St. Stephen's Cathedral features a distinctive tiled roof characterized by its colored zigzag pattern and prominent double-headed eagles.

question.leadin: The fates of the remnants of both the Holy Roman Empire and post-Napoleonic France were debated in this city.
question.text: Name this Austrian city, site of an 1814-1815 Congress.
question.clue: This event saw Krakow become a free city, and the Earl of Clancarty replaced Castlereagh as England's representative to this event.

swap.leadin: His death and that of his wife Sophie prompted the July Crisis.
swap.text: Name this heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne whose assassination in Sarajevo by Gavrilo Princip helped lead to the outbreak of World War I.
swap.clue: His wife was never permitted in the royal carriage, as a condition of his marriage to the lower-class woman after he became heir apparent following the death of his cousin Rudolf and father Charles Louis.

question.leadin: This conflict begin with the invasion of Silesia by Frederick the Great.
question.text: Name this war fought after the death of Charles VI.
question.clue: During this war, Prussia won the Battle of Mollwitz and seized Silesia, while led by Frederick the Great, whose invasion of a neighboring country violated the Pragmatic Sanction.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about some of the Revolutions of 1848.
swap.text: The Revolutions of 1848 shattered the delicate Concert of Europe established by this Austrian statesman to restore the European balance of power at the Congress of Vienna, which this leader hosted.
swap.clue: The Academic Legion forced this man's resignation during the Revolutions of 1848.

question.leadin: This empire was founded in the 1867 Ausgleich ("OWSS-glykh") and was dissolved in the Treaties of Saint Germain and Trianon ("TREE-uh-non").
question.text: Name this empire that was first ruled by Franz Josef I.
question.answerHtml: Austria-Hungary [or Austro-Hungarian Empire or Österreichisch-Ungarische Monarchie or Osztrák-Magyar Monarchia; prompt on dual monarchy; do not accept “Austria” or “Hungary” alone]
question.clue: This empire formed after the Ausgleich, which made Franz Joseph I its first emperor.

swap.text: This nephew of Franz Josef became heir presumptive after the suicide of Crown Prince Rudolf and his own father's death. His assassination by Bosnian nationalist Gavrilo Princip set off the July Crisis.
swap.clue: This nephew of Emperor Franz Joseph I, who was assassinated in Sarajevo in 1914. This man's death prompted the July Crisis, which eventually caused the escalations that led to World War I.

question.leadin: Answer the following about self-identified enlightened despots.
question.text: When asked his thoughts on the American Revolution, this Austrian ruler and enlightened despot replied, "Madam, it is my trade to be a King". This son of Maria Theresa liberalized the curriculum of the University of Vienna and abolished the Robot Patent.
question.clue: This ruler sent generals Lacy and Laudon on a series of tactical maneuvers in one conflict that saw little actual fighting, the War of Bavarian Succession, and, in response to the peasants' revolt of Horea, abolished serfdom.

swap.text: Following U [OO] Thant's resignation, this Austrian served as Secretary General a position he held until 1981. He went on to be President of Austria from 1968 to 1992.
swap.clue: His service in the Kozara mountains involved a massacre of Yugoslavs, and he was also a senior lieutenant during the deportation of forty thousand Jews from Salonika.

question.leadin: This man was the prime supporter of a bizarre scheme to build a Jewish homeland in Uganda.
question.text: Name this Austrian writer and statesman whose utopian novel The Old New Land contains his slogan, "If you will it, it is no dream". He wrote The Jewish State to articulate his growing conviction of the impossibility of Jewish assimilation.
question.clue: He could not overcome the opposition of the Russian faction of his confederates to the Uganda plan, nor could he talk the Ottoman Sultan into giving him what he wanted.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the 19th century "Great Game,"
swap.text: In a mildly related diplomatic move, the short-lived League of the Three Emperors united Russia's Alexander II, Germany's Kaiser Wilhelm I, and Austria under this ruler. During his long reign, Austria lost the Seven Weeks War to Prussia, and his nephew Franz Ferdinand was assassinated in 1914.
swap.clue: The Fundamental Articles of his minister of commerce and agriculture Albert Schaffle was denounced by German nationalists, and he appeared beside Alexander II in Berlin in 1873 in support of the Dreikaiserbund.

question.text: To help reconstruct Portugal's social structure after the earthquake, a queen regent with this name founded the Casa Pia children's educational institution. A later Braganza queen of this name was similarly known as "The Educator."
question.answerHtml: Maria [or Maria the Pious; or Maria the Mad; or Dona Maria I; or Maria the Good Mother; or Dona Maria II]

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the political impact of the death of Rudolf, Crown Prince of Austria, in the Mayerling Incident.
swap.text: As part of a murder-suicide pact, Rudolf killed this teenage lover of his in the Mayerling Incident.

question.leadin: Answer the following about setbacks for the Austro-Hungarian royal family which presumably made Emperor Franz Joseph I a very sad man.
question.text: The Black Hand plotted this incident, in which Gavrilo Princip murdered a visiting Archduke in Sarajevo. This event was a primary catalyst for World War I.
question.answerHtml: assassination of Franz Ferdinand [accept answers including synonyms for assassination such as "murder," "shooting," etc.]
question.clue: Centrally planned by a man known as "Apis," it may have been possible due to its central figure's morganatic marriage to Sophie Chotek, whose visibility was insisted upon.

swap.text: Your belief in Central Power unity was probably shattered following this affair late in the war. In this affair, Clemenceau published Emperor Charles I's correspondence with the namesake person asking for peace with the Allies.

question.leadin: This son of Leopold II was named commander-in-chief of the Austrian army in 1806.
question.text: Name this winner over Andre Massena at First Zurich. More famously, he became the first person to beat Napoleon in over a decade when he beat Napoleon at Aspern-Essling.

swap.leadin: This man's election was vetoed three times by Franz Joseph, who despised him.
swap.text: Name this mayor of Vienna from 1897 - 1910, whose virulent anti-semitism may have inspired a young Adolf Hitler.

question.leadin: This agreement created separate parliaments for a country's Cisleithanian and Transleithanian regions.
question.text: Name this 1867 compromise that was negotiated by Friedrich von Beust and signed by Franz Joseph I.
question.clue: Friedrich Ferdinand von Beust ("boyst") supported this event in a failed attempt to exact his revenge over a defeat at Koniggratz.

swap.leadin: After this event, Count Eduard Taaffe claimed that a man died "due to a rupture of an aneurism of the heart."
swap.text: What event was a murder-suicide in which a man shot his lover, Mary Vetsera, and then killed himself while staying at a hunting lodge in the village that lends its name to this event?
swap.clue: Ida von Ferenczy was drafted to break the news of this event to Empress Elizabeth.
